newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SAMPDORIA CHIEF FACES DISCIPLINARY ACTION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SAMPDORIA CHIEF FACES DISCIPLINARY ACTION.

text.p: Sampdoria general director Emiliano Salvarezza faces disciplinary action from the Italian soccer federation after he called a four-match ban given to Yugoslav defender Sinisa Mihajlovic "shameful and squalid".

The federation said on Thursday the comments were "damaging to the reputation of federal bodies and in particular the sporting judge whom he accused of partiality". Sampdoria were also reported as the club responsible.
Salvarezza, ironically a member of the league's judicial commission as well as the marketing commission, said that there was a conspiracy against his club.
"There seems to be a scientific plan to prevent us from playing in Europe," he told Italian newspapers.

The Yugoslav player was suspended after he was sent off in Sampdoria's 4-0 defeat by Atalanta on Sunday for kicking the ball in the direction of the referee after a penalty was awarded. Mihajlovic also swore at the official.
Salvarezza said that Mihajlovic's ban made him want to sell the player to AC Milan so that the suspension would be taken away because big clubs seemed immune from such sanctions.
Juventus striker Alen Boksic of Croatia was suspended for two games at the same time as Mihajlovic after being sent off against Internazionale on Sunday for kneeing an opponent in the face.
"Boksic hit an opponent and they gave him two days. Mihajlovic hit nobody and they gave him four. We want the rules to be the same for everybody," Salvarezza said.

Sampdoria were second in the league at the start of the month, a position that for the first time brings qualification to the European Cup at the end of the season. They are are now fourth after two consecutive defeats.
